item.title: Draft ministerial ordinance to extend mandatory electronic radio licensing filings to broadcasters
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications published a draft ministerial ordinance for public comment on 2026-11-28 to extend mandatory electronic filing for radio-station licensing and related procedures to core broadcasting station licensees. It would amend Article 51-9-2 of the Regulations for Enforcement of the Radio Act (Radio Regulatory Commission Rule No. 14 of 1950), under Article 102-19(1) of the Radio Act (Act No. 131 of 1950). The proposed extension excludes community broadcasters and operators of reception-interference countermeasure relay broadcasting stations or temporary disaster broadcasting stations; for covered licensees, it would also cover applications concerning other radio stations, including STL and FPU stations. The explanatory material envisages commencement on 2028-05-01, coinciding with the next mass relicensing application period, and distinguishes this proposal from electronic-filing requirements implemented for national government bodies, incorporated administrative agencies and mobile telephone operators and similar operators on 2026-04-01. The stated comment deadline is 2026-12-28 00:00 JST. Original title: 無線局の免許等関連手続の電子申請義務化に係る制度改正案に対する意見募集（電波法施行規則の一部を改正する省令案） Public Comment Open | e-Gov Public Comment | Published 2026-11-28 | First detected 2026-11-28 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: MLIT announces IMO talks on draft MARPOL amendments for shipping decarbonization
item.description: AI summary: Proposed MARPOL amendments include a fuel regulatory framework to progressively shift ships toward lower-GHG alternative fuels, supporting the IMO goal of zero GHG emissions from international shipping by around 2050. On 2026-11-27, Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism announced that MEPC 85 was scheduled for 2026-11-30 through 2026-12-04 in London to discuss agreement on further GHG reduction measures. Adoption deliberations had been postponed for one year following opposition from some countries; if agreement is reached, the second extraordinary MEPC session is scheduled to resume on 2026-12-04 to consider adoption. Other planned adoption discussions concern Ballast Water Management Convention annex amendments, MARPOL Annex I provisions on integrated bilge water treatment systems, MARPOL Annex VI provisions on crude oil tanker pressure/vacuum valves, and NOx Technical Code provisions on engines co-firing non-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia. Further discussions concern stronger performance verification testing for ballast water treatment systems and support for implementing the BBNJ Agreement. Original title: 国際海運のカーボンニュートラルのための国際条約の策定に向けて ～国際海事機関（ＩＭＯ） 第85回海洋環境保護委員会（11/30～12/4）の開催～ Government Announcement | Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) | Published 2026-11-27 | First detected 2026-11-28 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: Environment Minister's opinion on proposed Minamisatsuma wind power project
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of the Environment announced on 2026-11-27 the submission of the Environment Minister's opinion on the planning-stage environmental consideration document for the proposed Minamisatsuma Wind Power Project. Minamisatsuma Wind LLC proposes a wind farm in Minamisatsuma City, Kagoshima Prefecture, with capacity of up to 73,100 kW from up to 17 turbines of approximately 4,300 kW each. The opinion calls for field surveys and environmental assessment to inform site boundaries and equipment layouts, prioritizing avoidance or reduction of environmental impacts before considering compensation measures. It identifies concerns involving noise and turbine shadows near homes, schools and other sensitive facilities, sediment collapse or runoff, migratory raptors, and effects on scenic viewpoints and nature-based recreation. It also calls for coordination with relevant authorities, sufficient explanation to local residents, and documentation of the consideration process and results in the scoping document and subsequent environmental assessment documents. item.description: AI summary: The Cabinet Office published a consultation on 2026-11-27 on a draft Cabinet Office Ordinance amending the implementing regulations for satellite launches and management and for space-resource exploration and development activities, in connection with implementation of Act No. 39 of 2026 amending the satellite launch and management legislation and related laws. The package includes proposed revisions to a notice setting an amount determined by the Prime Minister, examination criteria and standard processing periods. It also covers revised guidelines for launch permits, launch-rocket type certification, launch-facility conformity certification, satellite-management permits, collision prevention, on-orbit servicing and third-party liability compensation, plus a draft guideline on conformity certification of satellites and other objects before loading.
